intro: Both take an X that stands out (a rank, an age, a season, a big occasion) and say what follows from it. ともなると looks up a scale: once you reach the level of X, things are generally different. とあって points at one special situation: because it is X, this is what happened. First question: is the sentence a general expectation, or a report of what was observed?

skills.rule: X ともなると / ともなれば Y: once it gets to the level of X, Y is what you would naturally expect.
skills.explain:
ともなると (and ともなれば, which means the same) follows a noun of rank, age, time or scale: 大学生, 社長, 十二月, 一流ホテル, 週末. It can also follow a verb in the dictionary form: 留学するともなると. X is a step up from the ordinary, and Y is what generally comes with that step: more responsibility, more people, a different standard.

Y is a general statement or expectation, usually in the non-past: 十二月ともなると、町はにぎやかになる. It is not a report of one past event. For "because it was a holiday, it was crowded that day", use とあって.

Compare として, which only states the role something acts in: 社長として発言する (speak as president). ともなると says what being at that level brings with it.
patterns: [rank / age] ともなると、[expected duty or behaviour]
[verb dictionary form] ともなると、[what it entails]

examples.jp: 十二月[じゅうにがつ]{ともなると}、町[まち]はどこもにぎやかになる。
examples.en: Once December comes, the whole town gets lively.

examples.jp: 大学生[だいがくせい]{ともなると}、自分[じぶん]のことは自分[じぶん]でしなければならない。
examples.en: Once you're a university student, you have to look after yourself.

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{ともなると}、この公園[こうえん]は家族[かぞく]連[づ]れでいっぱいになる。
examples.en: At weekends this park fills up with families.

examples.jp: 社長[しゃちょう]{ともなれば}、毎日[まいにち]のように会議[かいぎ]がある。
examples.en: When you're the company president, you have meetings almost every day.

examples.jp: 一流[いちりゅう]のホテル{ともなると}、サービスがまったく違[ちが]う。
examples.en: When it comes to a top-class hotel, the service is in another league.

examples.jp: 海外[かいがい]に住[す]む{ともなると}、準備[じゅんび]することがたくさんある。
examples.en: Actually moving abroad means there's a lot to prepare.

contrast.note: とあって reports one occasion and its observed result: 週末とあって、公園は混んでいた. ともなると states the general pattern: 週末ともなると、公園は混む.
として names a role: 社長として話す. It says nothing about what that level brings; ともなると does.
といえども goes against the expectation (even a president must follow the rules). ともなると goes with it.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]は日曜日[にちようび]{ともなると}、店[みせ]が混[こ]んでいた。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]は日曜日[にちようび]{とあって}、店[みせ]が混[こ]んでいた。
mistakes.note: One observed past occasion takes とあって; ともなると is for what generally happens.

mistakes.bad: 子[こ]ども{ともなると}、夜[よる]は早[はや]く寝[ね]る。
mistakes.good: 小学生[しょうがくせい]は夜[よる]早[はや]く寝[ね]る。
mistakes.note: X must be a step up on a scale; "child" is not a level you reach, so ともなると does not fit.

skills.tip: Can you say "once you get up to X, you'd expect ..."? Then ともなると.

skills.rule: X とあって Y: because it is the special situation X, Y happened, as you would expect.
skills.explain:
とあって follows a noun or the plain form of a verb or adjective, with no だ after a noun: 連休とあって, 人気歌手が来るとあって, 初めてとあって. X is a notable, one-off circumstance: a long weekend, a rare sale, a famous guest, a first time. Y is the natural, observed result, typically reported in the past: crowds, queues, excitement.

It has a reporting tone, like a news story. Y is a description, not the speaker's request, invitation or decision: 連休とあって、早く出かけましょう is wrong; use 連休なので. An ordinary cause (rain, a Monday) also sounds odd: X should be worth commenting on.

The related form とあれば means "if it is for X" and leads to a willingness: 子どものためとあれば、何でもする.
patterns: [famous person] が来るとあって、[crowds / excitement]
初めての [event] とあって、[nervous / excited]

examples.jp: 連休[れんきゅう]{とあって}、高速道路[こうそくどうろ]はひどく混[こ]んでいた。
examples.en: Because it was a long weekend, the motorway was badly jammed.

examples.jp: 年[ねん]に一度[いちど]のセール{とあって}、店[みせ]の前[まえ]には長[なが]い列[れつ]ができていた。
examples.en: Since it was the once-a-year sale, there was a long queue outside the shop.

examples.jp: 初[はじ]めての海外旅行[かいがいりょこう]{とあって}、娘[むすめ]は朝[あさ]からうれしそうだった。
examples.en: It was her first trip abroad, so my daughter looked happy from the morning on.

examples.jp: 人気[にんき]歌手[かしゅ]が来[く]る{とあって}、会場[かいじょう]には大勢[おおぜい]のファンが集[あつ]まった。
examples.en: With a popular singer coming, crowds of fans gathered at the venue.

examples.jp: 久[ひさ]しぶりの晴天[せいてん]{とあって}、公園[こうえん]は人[ひと]でいっぱいだった。
examples.en: Since it was the first sunny day in a while, the park was packed.

contrast.note: ともなると states a general expectation at a level: 年末ともなると忙しい. とあって reports this occasion: 年末とあって、駅は混雑していた.
ゆえに is a stiff, logical "therefore / because of" for any cause. とあって needs a special situation and an observed, natural reaction.
といえども is concessive: even with X, Y goes against expectation. とあって says Y is exactly what X leads you to expect.

mistakes.bad: 連休[れんきゅう]{とあって}、早[はや]めに出[で]かけましょう。
mistakes.good: 連休[れんきゅう]なので、早[はや]めに出[で]かけましょう。
mistakes.note: とあって cannot lead into a suggestion or request; use なので.

mistakes.bad: 大学生[だいがくせい]{とあって}、自分[じぶん]のことは自分[じぶん]でしなければならない。
mistakes.good: 大学生[だいがくせい]ともなると、自分[じぶん]のことは自分[じぶん]でしなければならない。
mistakes.note: A general rule about a level takes ともなると, not とあって.

skills.tip: Think of a news headline: "Long weekend, so the roads were packed." A special occasion plus an observed result is とあって.
